channel.title: Carillon blog
channel.description: Tips, strategy and behind-the-scenes posts about Carillon.

item.title: Seven beginner tips for Carillon: reach, sources and decoys
item.description: Seven practical tips for new Carillon players: hold before you tap, read the reach circles, find the dot nothing reaches, and see through the showy decoys.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: Calm by design: why Carillon has no timers, lives or energy
item.description: Carillon has no timers, no lives and no energy, and no ad ever interrupts a chain. Why we built a chain-reaction puzzle that waits for you, and where you will notice it.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: Chain reactions as graphs: the maths behind a Carillon tap
item.description: A Carillon field is a directed graph, a chain is a shortest-path search, and the fewest taps is the number of source components. The maths, explained plainly.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: How Carillon's levels are made: grown, proven, never repeated
item.description: Behind the scenes: how Carillon grows its fields, proves the fewest taps, measures difficulty in bits, and makes sure no two levels feel like the same one.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: How Carillon's hint works, and when to use it
item.description: Carillon's hint lights the best next tap from wherever the field is now: it dims the rest, sweeps out the dot's reach and outlines what its ring will pop.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: How to play Carillon: the rules in two minutes
item.description: Learn to play Carillon, the chain-reaction puzzle: tap a dot, its ring pops every dot it reaches, and each pop is a note. Hold first to read, then clear the field.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: Made by two: a human and an AI building a puzzle game
item.description: Carillon is made by a two-person team: Shravan Goswami and Claude Opus 5.5, an AI model by Anthropic. How the work is split, and a few stories from the build.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: How to get three stars in Carillon, and what the spare tap is for
item.description: How Carillon scores a level, why every level gives you one spare tap, and a simple method for finding the three-star read, with a worked two-tap example.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5

item.title: Why every pop is a note: the pentatonic idea behind Carillon
item.description: In Carillon a dot's colour is its note and its size is the octave, on a pentatonic scale, so any chain sounds like music. How the notes are chosen and made.
item.author: Shravan Goswami, Claude Opus 5.5
